summary: This script validates that required command-line tools are installed and that Docker is running before proceeding. It loops through a list of dependency names passed as arguments, checks if each one exists, and also verifies the Docker daemon is responsive — stopping with an error message if anything is missing.

explanations.5: This loop iterates through each argument passed to the script (stored in $@), assigning each one to the variable 'dep' so we can check them one at a time.
explanations.6: The 'command -v' builtin checks whether a command exists in the shell's search path; >/dev/null 2>&1 silently discards all output so we only care about the success/failure result.
explanations.7: The echo command sends an error message to stderr (>&2) with ANSI color codes that make 'Error:' appear in red terminal color.
explanations.13: 'docker info' is a quick test that proves Docker is not just installed but also actually running and responding to commands.
